name: Wu Fang
current_role: Director, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials (芳源股份, formerly Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR 688148)
profile: Wu Fang (吴芳) is a director and major shareholder of Guangdong Fangyuan (688148), a Jiangmen-based battery-materials maker, and a concerted-action party of controlling shareholder and chairman Luo Aiping. Per the Q1 2026 report she held ~17.3m shares (3.40%).
interesting_fact: Company filings list Wu Fang as an acting-in-concert party with founder Luo Aiping, who was re-elected chairman of the 4th board in July 2025 while Wu Fang joined that board.
notes: Low public profile; facts from search-result summaries of company filings. Route via company board office / IR (Fangyuan, 688148). Hurun list shares wealth with Luo Aiping.

name: Jin Liangshun
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Jingong Group (精功集团), Shaoxing; group underwent bankruptcy reorganisation from 2019
profile: Jin Liangshun (金良顺) built Shaoxing's Jingong (精功) group from a warp-knitting machinery factory into a ~50bn-yuan conglomerate spanning steel structures, equipment, new materials, yellow wine (Kuaijishan), general aviation and big data, controlling several listed companies. After a 2019 liquidity crisis the group was reorganised and in 2022 control of its listed assets passed to Fang Chaoyang.
interesting_fact: He took yellow-wine brand Kuaijishan (会稽山) through restructuring and onto the Shanghai exchange in 2014, alongside Jingong Steel Structure and Jingong Technology.
deep_cut_fact: He started at 14 as a carpenter (木工) at the Shaoxing Warp Knitting Machinery factory in the 1960s, rising to workshop head and factory director; press dubbed him the 'little carpenter' (小木匠).
notes: Alive as of Dec 2022 article (aged 68); no later confirmation. Sensitive: group collapsed/bankruptcy restructuring 2019-2022 — avoid in outreach. No published contacts found.

name: Zeng Min
current_role: CEO, Horizon Scientific Corp. (Irvine, CA); co-founder and former chairman (2018-Dec 2023) of Venus Medtech (Hangzhou) (HKEX 2500)
profile: Zeng Min (Min Frank Zeng) co-founded Venus Medtech in Hangzhou in 2009 with Eric Zi, developing transcatheter heart valve (TAVR) devices; he chaired the HK-listed company until December 2023. He has been CEO of Irvine-based Horizon Scientific since 2004 and previously sat on the board of LifeTech Scientific.
interesting_fact: Venus Medtech was an early Chinese developer of transcatheter aortic valve replacement devices; Zeng still held ~7.6% of its H shares as of mid-2026.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an undergraduate degree from Tsinghua University and a graduate degree from the University of Texas at Austin.
notes: US-based (Irvine). Venus Medtech had governance turmoil; avoid. Alive status inferred from 2026 shareholding records.

name: Wu Xian
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen WOTE Advanced Materials (沃特股份, SZSE 002886)
profile: Wu Xian (吴宪) is chairman of Shenzhen WOTE Advanced Materials, a high-performance polymer/specialty materials company founded in 2001 and listed in Shenzhen. Hurun lists his wealth jointly with He Zheng, WOTE's general manager and director.
interesting_fact: In WOTE's 2024 ESG report chairman's letter he framed the company's strategy as becoming a platform for high-performance materials.
notes: Current-role confirmation latest as of April 2025 ESG report. Route via WOTE board secretary/IR office (listed on cninfo).

name: Li Dezhi
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~60% as of Mar 2026), Chongqing Sifang New Material (四方新材, SSE 605122)
profile: Li Dezhi (李德志) is the largest individual shareholder of Chongqing Sifang New Material, a Banan-district ready-mixed concrete producer listed in Shanghai, whose revenue comes entirely from Chongqing. Hurun lists his wealth with Zhang Lilan.
interesting_fact: Ready-mix concrete made up about 90% of Sifang's 2025 revenue of 1.03bn yuan; management has said it is exploring 'new quality productive forces' for a transformation.
notes: Very low profile; personal bio not found. Company had 2025 loss. Route via Sifang board office/IR.

name: Jason Bannister
current_role: Founder and executive chairman, Oak Furniture Land (UK furniture retailer)
profile: Jason Bannister founded Oak Furniture Land in 2004 with about £10,000 of imported Mexican pine he sold on eBay, becoming eBay UK's top retailer before launching the website (2007), an airfield showroom (2009) and a Cheltenham store (2010). He grew it into a ~100-store chain, never taking outside investors, and later moved from MD to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Within four hours of his first eBay listings he had missed 80 phone calls; within two years he was eBay UK's largest retailer by turnover.
deep_cut_fact: His first taste of retail was a brief job at 15 in a golf club pro shop, followed by three years on the B&Q shop floor and about ten years at Walmsley Furniture; the £10,000 seed money had been saved for a house extension.
notes: Exec-chairman move reported by Retail Week (date not verified): https://www.retail-week.com/home-and-diy/oak-furniture-land-boss-becomes-chairman-amid-reshuffle/7028457.article. Route via Oak Furniture Land head office/press.

name: Narendra Bansal
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Intex Technologies (India) Ltd
profile: Born in 1963 in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, Narendra Bansal traded audio/video cassettes and then floppy disks and PC components in Delhi before founding International Impex (1994) and Intex Technologies (1996), which grew into a major Indian maker of mobile phones, consumer durables and IT accessories. He also owned IPL franchise Gujarat Lions.
interesting_fact: He started Intex with about Rs 20,000 and a single product, Ethernet cards; Intex later became one of India's top-selling mobile phone brands.
deep_cut_fact: He finished secondary school in Nepal, where his family had moved, before returning to Delhi in 1980 for a commerce degree at Delhi University; his first trade in the late 1980s was audio cassettes sold to Delhi market retailers.
notes: Active in TiE, Rotary and Rajasthan Club. Intex's current business scale not verified for 2026. Route via Intex corporate office.

name: Bart Becht
current_role: Former CEO of Reckitt Benckiser (1995-2011) and former partner at JAB Holding (2012-2019); investor and philanthropist
profile: Dutch-born Bart Becht (b. 1956) joined Benckiser in 1988 after Procter & Gamble, became CEO in 1995 and led the 1999 Reckitt & Colman merger, roughly quintupling Reckitt Benckiser's value before retiring in 2011. He then became a partner at JAB Holding (Keurig Dr Pepper, Krispy Kreme, Pret) and chaired Coty, retiring from JAB in 2019.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Reckitt Benckiser was the fourth-best performing FTSE 100 stock over the ten years to 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Becht Family Charitable Trust in 2006 (humanitarian, education and environmental causes incl. Save the Children), sat on Save the Children UK's board 2013-14 and ranked second on the Sunday Times Giving List in 2011.
notes: Coty chairmanship appears to have ended in 2018 (Peter Harf chair 2018-2025) per search-result governance data; current board seats not verified. Education: Groningen BA, Chicago Booth MBA. Low public profile since 2019.

name: Martin H. Nesbitt
current_role: Co-founder, Senior Partner, Co-Chairman & Co-CEO, The Vistria Group; director of Phoenix Education Partners, American Airlines Group and Chewy; Chair, Obama Foundation
profile: Chicago businessman Marty Nesbitt (b. 1962, Columbus, Ohio) co-founded The Parking Spot in 1998 with Penny Pritzker, building the first nationally branded airport-parking company before its 2011 sale. In 2013 he co-founded private-equity firm Vistria with Kip Kirkpatrick, investing in healthcare, education and financial services (incl. University of Phoenix parent Phoenix Education Partners).
interesting_fact: He chairs the Obama Foundation and was one of Barack Obama's earliest supporters and fundraisers from the start of his political career.
deep_cut_fact: An ABC Scholars placement took him to Columbus Academy, where basketball coach Jack MacMullan taught him to see himself as part of a team; his first job after college was at GM's Detroit HQ, and he names Stevie Wonder and Marvin Gaye among his music loves. His motto: 'It's not about me.'
notes: Chicago Booth MBA '89, Albion College. Best route via The Vistria Group (Chicago).
